title: Why We Numb Our Pain | Trauma, Alcohol & Emotional Avoidance

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们除了用时间换金钱之外还能赚钱，会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，临床心理学家，自2019年以来我一直在开发被动和循环收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个好消息要告诉大家。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现在已经开放报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，比如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于2022年完成了这个项目，此后也一直陪伴着两批心理学家走过了他们的学习旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的专属推广链接加入，你将获得苏菲的额外福利以及我个人的独家支持礼包，无需支付任何额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 其中包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四个小组圆桌大师班、大师课、个性化指导、一份Fortnum & Mason的美食奖励，以及限时的一对一教练辅导福利。

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 了解更多信息，请访问简介中链接的我的福利页面。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的福利。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，随时可以找我。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to Inner Work.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎来到“内心工作”。

sentences.en: I am Dr. Marianne Trent, a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: It's lovely to have you here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来到这里。

sentences.en: So in the main episode this week on psychology, actually, I was talking with Dr. Alex Button about all things EMDR and trauma.
sentences.zh: 所以在本周这期关于心理学的主节目中，实际上，我一直在和亚历克斯·巴顿博士探讨所有关于眼动脱敏再加工（EMDR）和创伤的话题。

sentences.en: And whilst the whole episode is really impactful, I thought we'd take a little bit of a deeper dive.
sentences.zh: 虽然整集内容都很有影响力，但我想我们可以更深入地探讨一下。

sentences.en: So it's that idea that sometimes as humans we will naturally be, you know, avoidant of pain.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那个概念：有时候作为人类，你知道的，我们会天生回避痛苦。

sentences.en: It makes sense because we need to be aversive to pain.
sentences.zh: 这很合逻辑，因为我们需要对痛苦产生厌恶感。

sentences.en: It's why when we are, you know, with young children, we'll say, you know, keep your hands away from the hob.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当我们和，你知道的，小孩子们在一起时，我们会说，你知道的，把手离炉子远一点。

sentences.en: Don't touch the oven.
sentences.zh: 不要碰烤箱。

sentences.en: Like, let's keep ourselves safe.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们要保护好自己。

sentences.en: But if we then do burn ourselves or hurt ourselves, we learn that that pain is not good.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们真的烧伤了自己或伤害了自己，我们就会明白那种痛苦是不好的。

sentences.en: I am recording this with a broken hand.
sentences.zh: 我是在手骨折的情况下录制这期节目的。

sentences.en: If you're watching on video, you might be like, has she not learned about pain being aversive?
sentences.zh: 如果你在看视频，你可能会想，她难道没学过痛苦具有厌恶性吗？

sentences.en: Um, I have, I have, I have learned and it will be interesting when I go back to do reformer Pilates, um, how that will lay flat for me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我学过，我学过了，而且等我回去做塑形普拉提时，看自己怎么平躺下来，这倒会挺有意思的。

sentences.en: I think I will be extra specially careful when I am pressing the pause button to do some more reps in between the exercises.
sentences.zh: 我想在两组动作之间按下暂停键去做更多重复次数时，我会格外格外小心。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I think especially as a trauma specialist, I definitely do need to be able to go back to the scene of the crime.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为特别是作为一名创伤专家，我确实需要能够重返犯罪现场。

sentences.en: And, uh, I broke my arm, uh, three years ago and I have been back cycling to the area where I hurt my arm because it felt important to reclaim that.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，我三年前摔断了胳膊，我已经重新骑车回到了我弄伤胳膊的那个地方，因为我觉得重新夺回主权很重要。

sentences.en: But of course, when it comes to psychological trauma, um, things that feel ouchie often, especially if we're feeling like we don't have somewhere safe to,
sentences.zh: 但当然，当谈到心理创伤时，呃，那些感觉有点疼的事情，通常情况下，尤其是如果我们觉得没有一个安全的地方去，

sentences.en: to take that or someone safe to take it to, then we can kind of build these little barriers in, in our brain or in our behavior so that we're not having to,
sentences.zh: 把这些带去，或者没有一个安全的人可以倾诉，那么我们就会在脑海中或行为上建立起这些小小的屏障，这样我们就不用，

sentences.en: to kind of address that so often.
sentences.zh: 那么经常去处理那种情绪了。

sentences.en: Um, because it's a natural kind of pain relief strategy and another way that, um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为这是一种天生的痛苦缓解策略，而另一种人们会这样做的方式是，

sentences.en: people will do that is to look for kind of some anesthetic to life and that might be ordinary life or it might be that there's,
sentences.zh: 去寻找某种生活的麻醉剂，那可能是平凡的生活，或者可能是其中存在着，

sentences.en: there's kind of trauma elements in there that might feel like they need more anesthetizing.
sentences.zh: 某种创伤元素，让人觉得需要更多的麻醉。

sentences.en: So sometimes when I'm working with people and they say, well, I don't drink, I don't do any drugs, I'm not on any medication, but I've got all of these things happening.
sentences.zh: 所以有时当我与人们交谈，他们说，嗯，我不喝酒，我不吸毒，我没吃任何药，但我身上发生了所有这些事情。

sentences.en: It's like, wow, well, how are you coping with that?
sentences.zh: 这就好像，哇，那你到底是怎么应付过来的？

sentences.en: Because you are doing all of that without anesthetic.
sentences.zh: 因为你这一切都是在没有麻醉剂的情况下做到的。

sentences.en: And that is not to say that I think that people would need that, but it's to kind of highlight that you are doing that, you know, um, without anything taking the edge off.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说我认为人们真的需要麻醉剂，而是为了强调，你知道的，你在没有任何东西来减轻痛苦的情况下，正在经历这一切。

sentences.en: So if it feels like it's a lot, that's because it is.
sentences.zh: 所以如果感觉压力很大，那是因为它确实很大。

sentences.en: Um, and of course, um, Alex put really nicely in the main podcast episode, um, that often, um, trauma can present as if it's anxiety or can present as if it's depression.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，呃，亚历克斯在主播客节目中说得很好，呃，通常情况下，呃，创伤表现出来的样子可能像是焦虑，或者可能像是抑郁。

sentences.en: And so it's going to make us kind of slow down, it's going to make us more hypervigilant, um, which might then make sleep harder as well.
sentences.zh: 所以它会让我们慢下来，让我们变得更加高度警惕，嗯，这反过来也可能会让睡眠变得更困难。

sentences.en: And sometimes, um, with depression, some people might retreat into sleep, but if you are traumatized, then being able to get that sleep is going to feel even trickier.
sentences.zh: 有时，呃，对于抑郁症，有些人可能会选择通过睡觉来逃避，但如果你受到了创伤，那么想要安然入睡就会感觉更加棘手。

sentences.en: And so often I'm working with people who will be saying, well, I am coping using alcohol or I'm using, you know, my prescribed medication.
sentences.zh: 因此，我经常接触到这样的人，他们会说，嗯，我靠酗酒来应付，或者我用，你知道的，医生开的处方药。

sentences.en: Sometimes I'm using a little bit more than has been prescribed.
sentences.zh: 有时我用的剂量比处方上开的要稍微多一点。

sentences.en: Please don't do that.
sentences.zh: 请不要那样做。

sentences.en: Please, if you find yourself in that position, do go and speak to your GP or your prescriber.
sentences.zh: 求你了，如果你发现自己处于那种境地，一定要去和你的全科医生或开处方的人谈谈。

sentences.en: But time and time again, people are telling me, well, I'll get in from work or I'll, you know, come five o'clock.
sentences.zh: 但一次又一次地，人们告诉我，嗯，我下班回家后，或者，你知道的，到了五点钟。

sentences.en: I'll find myself reaching for the fridge, reaching for the wine, reaching for the beer because I can't carry on with this level of thoughts, with this level of intrusion,
sentences.zh: 我会发现自己忍不住去拉开冰箱门，去拿红酒，去拿啤酒，因为我无法再承受这种程度的思绪，这种程度的侵扰，

sentences.en: with feeling this awful.
sentences.zh: 以及这种糟糕透顶的感觉。

sentences.en: And so it's that kind of seeking to, to change your feeling state, to change your mood state, to change the way you feel.
sentences.zh: 所以这其实就是那种试图去改变你的情感状态、改变你的情绪状态、改变你感受方式的行为。

sentences.en: And often when we're looking at the window of tolerance, it's that desire to bump yourself either in or out of a different mood state.
sentences.zh: 通常当我们审视容忍窗口时，那就是一种想要把自己撞进或撞出一个不同情绪状态的渴望。

sentences.en: So if we were looking at, if someone was feeling really spacey and numb and frozen and dissociated,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们看一下，如果有人觉得非常空虚、麻木、呆滞和解离，

sentences.en: then sometimes they will tell me that they will be looking at something to bump them up a bit so that they feel more normal.
sentences.zh: 那么有时他们会告诉我，他们会寻找能让自己稍微兴奋一点的东西，好让他们感觉更正常。

sentences.en: Or the other way around, if they're so hyper aroused and agitated, they'll be looking for something to bring them down.
sentences.zh: 或者反过来，如果他们高度亢奋且烦躁不安，他们就会寻找能让自己平静下来的东西。

sentences.en: And that's where alcohol might often be mentioned.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们经常会提到酒精。

sentences.en: But of course, doing this is kind of telling the brain, telling the body that we can't safely exist in the normal window of tolerance bit.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这样做其实是在告诉大脑、告诉身体，我们无法安全地存在于正常的容忍窗口之内。

sentences.en: And so this is where accessing therapy of some descriptions such as EMDR can be really powerful because it helps you to live that fuller life where you're more engaged,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么接受某种形式的治疗（如EMDR）会非常强大，因为它能帮助你过上更充实的生活，让你更有参与感，

sentences.en: where things feel like they come more easily to you.
sentences.zh: 让你觉得事情做起来更容易。

sentences.en: That might be your own career, that might be parenting, that might be just the thing that makes you, you.
sentences.zh: 那可能是你自己的职业生涯，可能是育儿，也可能只是那个让你成为独一无二的你的事物。

sentences.en: So if you feel that you are suffering with kind of managing post-trauma, please do know that it can be different.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你觉得自己在应对创伤后应激方面备受煎熬，请务必知道，情况是可以有所改变的。

sentences.en: People often will believe there's no hope for ever feeling any different when it comes to trauma.
sentences.zh: 人们往往会认为，在面对创伤时，永远感觉不到任何改变是没有希望的。

sentences.en: But I know, and Dr. Alex would want you to know, it absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 但我知道，亚历克斯博士也希望你知道，绝对是有希望的。

sentences.en: Change is possible.
sentences.zh: 改变是可能的。

sentences.en: I hope you found this special episode of Inner Work helpful.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得这期“内心工作”的特别节目对你有所帮助。

sentences.en: I love your thoughts and your feelings on it.
sentences.zh: 我很想听听你对此的想法和感受。

sentences.en: Please do let me know in the comments or by coming to connect with me on social media where I'm Dr. Marianne Trent everywhere.
sentences.zh: 请务必在评论区告诉我，或者在社交媒体上与我联系，我在所有平台上都叫“玛丽安·特伦特博士”。

sentences.en: If you like my episodes, if you like the content, please do share.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢我的节目，如果你喜欢这些内容，请务必分享。

sentences.en: Please do tag so that we can help Psychology Actually and Inner Work to develop a wider audience.
sentences.zh: 请务必加标签，以便我们帮助《实际上是心理学》和“内心工作”吸引更多受众。

sentences.en: That means we get even better guests every time.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们每一次都能请到更好的嘉宾。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I'll be along for the next episode of Inner Work, which will drop on Wednesday evenings in the UK.
sentences.zh: 我将会在下一期的“内心工作”中与大家见面，该节目将于英国时间的周三晚上发布。

sentences.en: Thank you again.
sentences.zh: 再次感谢。

sentences.en: Take care.
sentences.zh: 保重。
